sections.h2: Which sale route moves fastest for a Brookhaven seller?
sections.html:
Pace varies by route. An as-is buyer with cash can set the closing day with you, whereas a listing waits on showings, an appraisal and the buyer's mortgage. Money at stake is large: the 2020-2024 midpoint for a Brookhaven owner-occupied house is $692,700, about twice the $332,700 U.S. figure, so one percentage point of price is a lot of dollars.

  • Full listing: strongest exposure, plus staging, repair lists and the lender's calendar.
  • Owner-handled sale: no commission to pay, but buyers, contracts and disclosures are yours to manage.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer steps and no repair demands, normally at a figure below a polished listing.

Below, the page turns to what is particular to Brookhaven: its short history, housing numbers, permit rules, code-enforcement habits and the county tax process.

sections.h2: When did Brookhaven become a city?
sections.html:
Brookhaven is a DeKalb County city that incorporated in December 2012, and its police department opened for service on July 31, 2013. The Census Bureau counts 11.69 square miles of land, with a 2020 density near 4,720 residents for each square mile.

The city operates 19 parks, three swimming pools, two recreation centers and a community building on 352 acres of parkland. Water and sewer come from DeKalb County, and DeKalb's watershed department staffs a 24-hour emergency line at 770-270-6243. Rules on short-term rentals, building permits and construction hours come from the city's own code, so look at Brookhaven's pages, not the county's, when you plan work on a house here.

sections.h2: What do the latest Census figures show for Brookhaven?
sections.html:
The estimate for mid-2025 is 59,643 residents, 5.1 percent above the April 2020 estimates base, living in 24,271 households that average 2.36 people. Owners occupy 52.6 percent of homes.

  • House value, owner midpoint: $692,700.
  • Monthly owner outlay with a mortgage, midpoint: $3,141.
  • Rent including utilities, midpoint: $1,882.
  • Household income, midpoint, 2024 dollars: $117,663.
  • One-way commute: 25.1 minutes on average.

Each figure is from the Census table for Brookhaven and covers the whole city, so one house may sit far off the midpoint. About 71 percent of adults finished college, 21.1 percent of residents were born abroad and 29.2 percent use another language at home, which gives the buyer and tenant pool a wide mix of backgrounds.

Yes, though only for a resident owner holding a permit. Council adopted the Short-Term Rental Ordinance on April 23, 2019, and each permitted house may be rented no more than 180 days per year.

  • The applicant must have owned the property for over a year and hold a current DeKalb homestead exemption.
  • No permit goes to a business entity such as an LLC, a partnership or a family trust.
  • One owner, one permit, and permits are limited to five percent of residential parcels in each council district.
  • The permit costs $25 for one year and renews annually.

The rule that matters most to a seller: the permit ends when the property changes hands, so a buyer who wants a rental starts a fresh application. For permits that predate October 24, 2023, a new owner has six months after title transfer to apply without being turned away on the district cap. Ask Community Development how your council district stands before you pitch the house to investors.

sections.h2: What permits and work hours apply when preparing a Brookhaven house?
sections.html:
Construction or redevelopment of any kind needs a city permit, issued by the Community Development Department. Georgia contractor licensing applies, so contractors present a state license, whereas a homeowner working on their own house can sign a notarized Homeowner Affidavit.

The city asks applicants to wait 10 business days for review before calling about status, and its fee schedule lists the minimum and review fees, which use the ICC data valuation table. Complaints about work outside permitted hours go to police through 911: the city lists before 7 am or after 7 pm Monday to Friday, before 8 am or after 5 pm on Saturday, and all day Sunday. Residents can also report construction without a permit, and tree removal without one, through the Brookhaven Connect app, so close out permits on finished work before a buyer's inspector asks about it.

sections.h2: How do DeKalb assessments and homestead dates work for Brookhaven owners?
sections.html:
DeKalb County, not the city, appraises Brookhaven homes. Its appraisal department prints the formula as fair market value times 40 percent. An owner who disputes the value, the recorded property features or a homestead denial has 45 days from the notice date to appeal.

Three appeal paths exist. The Board of Equalization costs nothing and uses a three-member panel. A hearing officer is available at no filing fee for non-homestead property over $500,000. Non-binding arbitration needs a certified appraisal at the owner's expense and a $217 filing fee. Online filing uses the access code printed on the notice, and mailed appeals go to 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

sections.h2: What does Brookhaven code enforcement look at before a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Brookhaven Connect app lets neighbors report problems, and the list reads like a pre-listing checklist: tall grass or vegetation, trash or outside storage, inoperable vehicles and junk cars, illegal dumping, graffiti, construction without a permit and tree removal without a permit. A house with an open complaint can slow a buyer's lender or surprise a cash buyer, so walk the lot and clear these items first.

Police dispatch runs through ChatComm, so 911 doubles as the non-emergency line, and the police page lists no separate non-emergency number. The city's mapping team, part of Information Technology, won a 2014 URISA award for its work, and its parcel and land-use maps help you check zoning and boundaries before you list. Ask Community Development about any open permit or violation on your address; unresolved items are far easier to clear before a contract than after.

sections.h2: How is a Brookhaven sale reported and recorded?
sections.html:
A deed cannot go on record in DeKalb County until Georgia's transfer tax is settled. The sale is reported on Form PT-61, filed electronically through the clerks' cooperative's portal. The state's rate: $1 up to the first $1,000 of price, then 10 cents for every additional $100 or part of $100, with the seller liable unless the contract says differently.

On whether a particular deed is exempt, the state refers people to the county clerk. Filing trouble goes to the cooperative's support line at 800-304-5174, and whoever runs your closing normally files the form.

faqs.a: No. It incorporated in December 2012, and its police department began work on July 31, 2013, so Brookhaven counts among Georgia's youngest cities, set in DeKalb County.

faqs.q: What is the midpoint home value in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: $692,700 for owner-occupied homes, per the 2020-2024 Census data. Your house may price above or below that figure.

faqs.q: Will a new buyer inherit my short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. Brookhaven's ordinance ends the permit when ownership changes. Permits go only to owner-occupants with a DeKalb homestead exemption who have owned the property for more than a year.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a DeKalb value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. Use the access code on the notice to file online, or post the appeal to DeKalb County Property Appraisal, 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

faqs.q: Who pays Georgia's transfer tax at a Brookhaven closing?
faqs.a: The seller, by default, and a contract can move it to the buyer. It is paid ahead of recording, with PT-61 filed online.
